stem: At the patient's request, one DEA-registered retail pharmacy is asked to transfer an unfilled electronic MS Contin prescription to another DEA-registered retail pharmacy. Which pathway applies?

choices.text: Print the electronic prescription and fax the image.
Transfer it repeatedly while no quantity has been dispensed.
Have technicians at both pharmacies complete the transfer without pharmacist communication.
Use a one-time pharmacist-to-pharmacist electronic transfer after confirming state permission and federal compliance.
Treat the transaction as a Schedule II refill at the receiving pharmacy.

explanation.core_reasoning: Use a one-time pharmacist-to-pharmacist electronic transfer after confirming state permission and federal compliance. By contrast, 'Print the electronic prescription and fax the image.' uses a legal trigger absent from the stem.

choice_analysis.A: This near-miss uses a different trigger: Print the electronic prescription and fax the image.
choice_analysis.B: This near-miss uses a different trigger: Transfer it repeatedly while no quantity has been dispensed.
choice_analysis.C: This near-miss uses a different trigger: Have technicians at both pharmacies complete the transfer without pharmacist communication.
choice_analysis.D: The stated facts support this result: Use a one-time pharmacist-to-pharmacist electronic transfer after confirming state permission and federal compliance.
choice_analysis.E: This near-miss uses a different trigger: Treat the transaction as a Schedule II refill at the receiving pharmacy.

related_facts: morphine (MS Contin) is used for severe and persistent pain requiring extended opioid treatment; it is federal Schedule II and Massachusetts Schedule II.

At a patient's request, an unfilled electronic Schedule II through V prescription may be transferred once between DEA-registered retail pharmacies if allowed by state law, kept electronic, unaltered, and communicated directly between pharmacists.
explanation.mpje_trap: Reject 'Print the electronic prescription and fax the image.' because its legal trigger is absent.

reasoning_steps: Classify morphine under the federal and Massachusetts schedules before selecting a legal pathway
Match the scenario's operative facts to One-time transfer of electronic controlled prescriptions
Reject nearby rules whose schedule, trigger, deadline, or actor differs from Electronic prescriptions
